question: According to the manual, one out of every how many motorcycle crashes results in head or neck injuries?
explanation: The manual states one out of every five motorcycle crashes results in head or neck injuries.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.8, 'Helmet Use'

question: A study of more than 900 motorcycle crashes found that a DOT-compliant helmet:
choice_a: Blocked riders' peripheral vision in most cases
choice_b: Did not prevent even one rider from spotting danger to the sides
choice_c: Was the leading cause of crashes
choice_d: Reduced hearing enough to cause additional crashes
explanation: A study of more than 900 crashes, where 40% of riders wore helmets, did not find even one case where a helmet kept a rider from spotting danger.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.8, 'Helmet Use'

question: At speeds under 30 mph, a helmet can reduce the number and severity of head injuries by about:
explanation: At speeds below 30 mph, which is where most crashes occur, helmets can cut both the number and severity of head injuries by half.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.8, 'Helmet Use'

question: Helmeted riders are how many times more likely to survive head injuries compared to unhelmeted riders?
explanation: No matter the speed, helmeted riders are three times more likely to survive head injuries than those not wearing a helmet at the time of the crash.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.8, 'Helmet Use'

question: A helmet with a label from which organization gives additional assurance of quality beyond DOT compliance?
choice_c: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration
explanation: Helmets with a label from the Snell Memorial Foundation give an assurance of quality in addition to DOT and state standards.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.8-9, 'Helmet Selection'

question: A motorcycle windshield is:
choice_a: An acceptable substitute for a face shield or goggles
choice_b: Not a substitute for a face shield or goggles for eye protection
choice_c: Required by law on all motorcycles
explanation: A windshield is not a substitute for a faceshield or goggles; most windshields will not protect the eyes from wind.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9, 'Eye and Face Protection'

question: Tinted eye protection should NOT be worn:
explanation: The manual specifically warns that tinted eye protection should not be worn when little light is available.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9, 'Eye and Face Protection'

question: Riding gloves should be made of:
choice_b: Any material, as long as they are colorful
explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or similar durable material to protect the hands and improve grip.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9-10, 'Clothing'

question: Why does the manual recommend wearing a jacket even in warm weather?
explanation: A jacket should be worn even in warm weather to prevent dehydration; many are designed to protect without overheating the rider.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9, 'Clothing'

question: Boot or shoe heels for riding should be:
choice_a: Very tall for better ankle support
choice_b: Kept short so they do not catch on rough surfaces
choice_c: Made of soft rubber for comfort
explanation: Heels should be kept short so they do not catch on rough surfaces, and laces should be tucked in so they won't catch on the motorcycle.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9, 'Clothing'

question: More than half of all crashes involve riders with how much experience on their particular motorcycle?
explanation: More than half of all crashes involve riders with less than five months of experience on their motorcycle.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9, 'Borrowing and Lending'

question: If you must ride a borrowed or unfamiliar motorcycle, the manual advises you to:
choice_a: Ride at highway speed immediately to get used to it
choice_b: Skip the pre-ride checks since it isn't your motorcycle
choice_c: Avoid using the mirrors until familiar with the bike
choice_d: Make all the checks you would on your own motorcycle and ride cautiously
explanation: When using an unfamiliar motorcycle, make all the checks you would make on your own, find the controls, and ride cautiously with extra room for stopping.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.10-11, 'Get Familiar with the Motorcycle Controls'

question: In the pre-ride 'T-CLOCS' inspection, the 'T' stands for:
explanation: T stands for Tires and Wheels: check inflation pressure, treadwear, and general condition, and try the front and rear brake levers.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.11, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: In the pre-ride inspection, the 'C' for Controls includes checking:
choice_b: The clutch, throttle, horn, and mirrors
explanation: Controls checks include making sure the clutch and throttle operate smoothly, trying the horn, and cleaning/adjusting mirrors.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.11, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: In the pre-ride inspection, the 'S' stands for:
explanation: S stands for Stands: ensure the side stand operates smoothly and the spring holds it up, and the center stand (if equipped) is held firmly against the frame while moving.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.12, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: With the fuel valve closed before starting out, a motorcycle:
choice_d: May start on fuel remaining in the lines but will stall once it is used up
explanation: With the fuel valve closed, the motorcycle may start with fuel still in the lines but will stall once the lines are empty.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.11, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: Adjusting a mirror properly may show:
choice_a: The edge of your arm or shoulder along with the road behind and to the side
explanation: A properly adjusted mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and to the side is what matters most.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.11, 'Check Your Motorcycle'

question: Regarding responsibility for a crash, the manual explains that:
choice_a: Only the driver who violated a signal is ever at fault
choice_b: Both parties in a crash can typically claim some responsibility
choice_c: Crashes are always purely accidental with no fault
choice_d: Motorcyclists are never at fault in a car-motorcycle crash
explanation: The manual explains that in most crashes, both parties involved can claim some responsibility for what took place.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.13, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: As part of riding responsibly, the manual advises riders to search their path of travel how far ahead?
explanation: Riders are advised to search their path of travel 12 seconds ahead as part of managing responsibility and risk.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.13, 'Know Your Responsibilities'

question: The right motorcycle for a beginner should:
choice_b: Have a windshield installed regardless of fit
choice_c: Be borrowed from a friend to save money
choice_d: Fit the rider so the feet reach the ground and controls are easy to operate
explanation: Your motorcycle should 'fit' you: feet should reach the ground while seated, and controls should be easy to operate; smaller motorcycles are usually easier for beginners.
source_note: TDLR Motorcycle Operator Training Manual 2020-2021, p.9, 'The Right Motorcycle For You'
